release_contents: Three things shipped across this session's institutional deploys (builds 01a0fc5e, 01a0fc6c, 01a0fded): (1) PRIORITY 1 placement — the carousel is the hero's right-hand media card, replacing the static dawn poster in that grid cell (poster still renders when no slides are published), copy and CTA left, copy-then-media on mobile; images are shown WHOLE (object-fit contain over a blurred copy of themselves) because cover was clipping the owner's wide poster; slide 0 is eager+high priority (LCP) and later slides have no until reached (loading=lazy alone did nothing — all slides are stacked inside the viewport so the browser fetched them all); touch swipe, reduced-motion, pause. (2) PRIORITY 1.1 — POST /api/revalidate (HMAC-signed, allow-listed tag, constant-time compare, 5-minute replay window, bare 401 on every failure, revalidateTag with expire:0). proxy.ts matcher now excludes api/ — without that the route is rewritten to /bn/api/revalidate and 404s, silently. (3) A pre-existing bug found by browser QA — see prefetch_storm.
build_failure_and_fix: The first two build attempts of commit dcccebe (uuid 01a0f650-435b-7220-86e8-04c3bd1e80ca, then a verbatim retry 01a0f68c-1aa6-7260-a840-9244d1a0991f) FAILED deterministically on Hostinger's Node build server with a TurbopackInternalError while processing app/globals.css, both times bottoming out in the identical signature: Turbopack spawning a subprocess to run PostCSS/Tailwind's loader, and that subprocess 'exiting before we could connect to it with exit status: 0'. The exact same source built with zero errors on this session's local machine using the identical package.json/lockfile/Next.js 16.3.4+Turbopack, which ruled out a genuine code or dependency defect. hosting_nodejs_analyse-failed-build's AI diagnosis (suggesting dependency version bumps to @tailwindcss/postcss/eslint/next) was deliberately NOT trusted on faith and was not what fixed this — it was inconsistent with the successful local build on the same dependency versions. Root cause investigation instead followed the build log's OWN deprecation warning ('The middleware file convention is deprecated. Please use proxy instead') and the fact that the crash traced through Turbopack's MiddlewareEndpoint machinery. Fix attempt 1 (commit 548f658): ran Next's own `@next/codemod middleware-to-proxy` migration (middleware.ts -> proxy.ts, middleware() -> proxy() export, matcher/logic untouched) — rebuilt and FAILED AGAIN, with the identical crash signature reached via a different internal path (MiddlewareEndpoint::node_chunk instead of ::edge_chunk_group), proving the rename alone didn't change the underlying Turbopack machinery. Fix attempt 2 (commit 69041c2, the one that actually worked): forced the production build to use webpack instead of Turbopack (package.json's build script changed from `next build` to `next build --webpack`, a first-party supported flag, not a workaround) — this sidesteps Turbopack's subprocess-spawning loader-evaluation path entirely. Verified identical build output locally (same 42 routes, same postbuild route-manifest check) before redeploying; the resulting Hostinger build (uuid 01a0f69d-3c94-70ea-84a4-c287180b7c28) completed successfully. next dev still uses Turbopack by default — only the production build was changed. Conclusion: this was a Hostinger-build-container-specific limitation on whatever Turbopack's loader-evaluation subprocess needs (likely process-spawn or /tmp-exec related), not a bug in this codebase's CSS or the proxy/middleware convention itself — worth retrying `next build` (without --webpack) on some future Next.js/Turbopack version to see if this is fixed upstream before assuming --webpack must stay forever.

prefetch_storm.summary: The Bangla homepage (/, rewritten by proxy.ts to /bn) fell into an endless Next.js prefetch loop on roughly 2 of 3 page loads: fetch /about?_rsc=..., finish, find the entry stale, fetch again, at the speed of one round trip, never stopping. ~10 requests/second per open tab in production, ~280/second locally. English homepage and every other page: 12 of 12 loads clean. Reproduced with NO carousel and NO API data (4,000+ requests/14s, 4 of 4 runs), so it predates the carousel and this session; the first baseline run today already showed the aborted ?_rsc= requests. Invisible to curl (HTML returns in 0.17s), to the HTTP status, to the console, and often to a single screenshot run.
prefetch_storm.isolation: Hiding the one hero <a href=/about> stopped a live storm (347 fetches in 3s -> 0) even with the footer and header /about links still visible, but other links were seen joining the loop, so fixing one link would not fix the class. Root cause inside Next's segment-cache scheduler on a rewritten root was NOT identified — the workaround removes the trigger, not the underlying framework behaviour.
prefetch_storm.fix: components/SiteLink.tsx = next/link with prefetch defaulting to false; all 27 files that imported next/link now import it (one line each). Costs ~nothing here: a prefetch only warms a route up to its nearest loading boundary, there are zero loading.tsx files, every route is dynamic and the prefetch response is no-store, so there was nothing for it to have fetched — only ~15 extra server round trips per page load per visitor. __tests__/no-raw-next-link.test.mts fails the build if next/link is imported directly again.
prefetch_storm.evidence: Same local machine, same page: 2,300-4,600 requests per 14s on every run -> 0 on all six. PRODUCTION: scripts/request-storm-qa.mjs was RED against the old build (4 of 5 loads stormed, 157-431 requests, exit 1) and is GREEN against the fix (8 of 8 loads settled, exactly 23 requests each, 0 RSC, nothing after 6s). EN root and two inner pages also settle. Navigation re-verified on production in Chrome — click-through, Back, language switch across the rewrite, both languages: 13/13.
prefetch_storm.revisit: If Next is upgraded, or loading.tsx boundaries are added, re-test with scripts/request-storm-qa.mjs before restoring prefetching anywhere (pass prefetch explicitly on a Link to opt in).

volunteer_submit_2026_10_04.cloudflare_waf_finding: Cloudflare's Free Managed Ruleset rule 3114709a3c3b4e3685052c7b251e86aa ("React - Leaking Server Functions - CVE-2025-55183") refuses, with a bare 403 from the edge, any request that has a Next-Action header and whose first 1 MiB contains the bytes `"$F` or `'$F`. Binary uploads contain them by chance ~once per 8 MB: ~11.8% of uploads >= 1 MiB, always the same file. Measured with probes to an invalid action id (nothing runs): same body without the header never refused; random 1 MiB bodies 4/40 refused; a planted marker was seen up to byte 1,048,576 and not beyond. Fixed for the volunteer form by moving its JavaScript path to a plain route; verified in real Chrome: the very 826 KB photo that was refused on the Server Action path (4/4 attempts) is accepted. The four other upload forms (committee registration, committee correction, membership application, member profile) were exposed the same way and were moved in the next release — see upload_forms_2026_10_04.

Every commit SHA recorded in this file, and in the release manifests on the server, is the PRE-rewrite SHA. The commits are unchanged apart from those two paths and map as below. build-release.sh only reads `commit` here as a string for the manifest and requires the commit being BUILT to be an ancestor of origin/main, so the next deploy is unaffected; the next deploy should record the new SHA as usual.
